Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a compact, self-contained QA training case from the June 12 Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet. Show that source completeness and claim readiness are separate judgments, identify the sections that passed source-completeness review, explain the maturity-dependent exception including its cohort type and size and available leading read, and state the limits of what the packet decided. Title the document `Board-source QA case — Q2 source completeness vs claim readiness`.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Board-source QA case — Q2 source completeness vs claim readiness", "body": "# Board-source QA case — Q2 source completeness vs claim readiness

**Source:** June 12 Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet

## QA distinction

- **Source completeness** asks whether the required evidence fields and owner-supplied documentation are present—for example, the source owner, denominator or exact coverage dates, measurement limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence location.
- **Claim readiness** is a separate judgment about whether the evidence supports a particular board claim. Complete source fields do not by themselves establish a complete outcome window, approve a claim, or make a lane board-ready.

## Review result

**Passed source-completeness review:**

- **Expansion Assist** — required source fields were present, including the exposure denominator/coverage, limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence location.
- **Pricing-page path quality** — required source fields were present, including exact coverage, limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence location.
- **CS auto-nudge controls** — required source fields were present, including exact coverage, limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence location.

These were source-complete *preparation sections*, not claim approvals or board-readiness decisions.

## Maturity-dependent exception: Helio Start

The packet recorded a **fixed paid cohort of 50 workspaces** and an available leading read: **39 of 50 had completed a first integration by day 7**. That early operational read did not substitute for the mature customer-outcome row. The row remained incomplete because **not all 50 workspaces had complete day-90 windows**. Thus, source material could report the fixed cohort and day-7 read while mature outcomes were still unavailable; the packet did not establish a mature Helio Start claim.

## What the packet did—and did not—decide

The packet documented source completeness for the three sections above and the maturity gap for Helio Start. It **made no claim, closed no lane, and made no board-readiness decision**. In particular, a source-completeness pass must not be restated as approval of a causal, revenue, forecast, or other board claim.", "folder": null}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_134_02", "path": "args", "criterion": "The document identifies Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and CS auto-nudge as the three source-complete sections, and conveys that each had its required source owner, denominator or exact coverage fields, measurement limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence location, with no required source field missing. Missing any section or materially misstating why it was source-complete must fail.

The document states that Helio Start had a fixed paid cohort of exactly 50 workspaces and a complete leading read of exactly 39 of 50 reaching first integration by day 7, while its mature customer-outcome row remained incomplete because all 50 did not yet have complete day-90 windows. It must not portray the day-7 result as a mature outcome.

The document clearly teaches that source completeness and claim or board readiness are separate judgments, and states that the June 12 packet itself made no claim, closed no lane, and made no board-readiness decision. ## QA distinction

- **Claim readiness** is a separate judgment about whether the evidence supports a particular board claim. Complete source fields do not by themselves establish a complete outcome window, approve a claim, or make a lane board-ready.

- **Expansion Assist** — required source fields were present, including the exposure denominator/coverage, limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence location.
- **Pricing-page path quality** — required source fields were present, including exact coverage, limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence location.
- **CS auto-nudge controls** — required source fields were present, including exact coverage, limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence location.
